en.name: Chayote shoots
en.summary: Chayote shoots are the young tips and curled tendrils of the chayote vine, sold in bundles and stir-fried with garlic. No published figure exists for them, so treat them like tender salad greens: about 2–4 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, stored unwashed and loosely packed.
en.pantry: These are the youngest, thinnest growth on the plant, and they have no room-temperature storage life worth naming. In a warm kitchen the curled tendrils go limp within hours and brown at the tips by the end of the day. Take the bundle home and refrigerate it immediately; on a hot day, a cool bag for the trip makes a visible difference to what you unpack.
en.fridge: Store the shoots unwashed and loosely packed in a perforated bag in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and wash them only just before cooking. About 2–4 days is the working limit — borrowed from the published rule for tender salad greens, since nobody has published a figure for chayote shoots themselves. The curled tendrils go limp and brown first, so judge the bundle by them. Do not pack the bag tight: crushed stems bruise and the bruises turn slimy.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for chayote shoots and freezing them is not worth doing. Their whole appeal is the snap of the young stem and the crispness of the tendril, and freezing destroys both — you would thaw a wet green mass. Nothing unsafe would happen, but there would be nothing left to stir-fry. Buy the amount you will cook that evening; this is not a vegetable to stock up on.
spoilage: Tendrils gone limp and brown, then black at the tips
Slimy or darkened stems, especially where the bundle was tied
A sour or fermented smell when the bag is opened
tips: Buy bundles with tightly curled, bright green tendrils — that is the freshness test.
Snap the stems and discard any part that bends instead of breaking.
Store unwashed and loosely packed; wash just before cooking.
Stir-fry fast over high heat with garlic; long cooking turns them grey and slippery.

faq.q: How long do chayote shoots last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, unwashed and loosely packed in a perforated bag. That figure is borrowed from the rule for tender salad greens; none is published for the shoots themselves.
There is no timeline and no point. Freezing destroys the crisp tendrils and stems that are the entire reason to buy them.

faq.q: How do you tell if chayote shoots are fresh?
faq.a: Look at the tendrils: tightly curled and bright green means fresh, limp and browning means old. Then snap a stem — it should break cleanly rather than bend.

faq.q: Do you need to remove the tough stems?
faq.a: Yes. Snap each stem at the point where it breaks cleanly; anything below that will stay fibrous no matter how long you cook it.

zh.name: 龍鬚菜
zh.summary: 龍鬚菜是佛手瓜藤的嫩梢和捲鬚，通常成把販售，最常見的吃法是蒜炒。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照嫩葉沙拉菜來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 2～4 天，不清洗、鬆鬆裝袋。
zh.pantry: 這是整株植物上最嫩最細的部分，沒有值得一提的常溫保存期。在溫暖的廚房裡，捲鬚幾小時就軟垂，當天傍晚尖端就開始發褐。買回家請立刻冷藏；天熱時用保冷袋帶回家，打開時的差別看得出來。
zh.fridge: 不清洗、鬆鬆裝進打洞袋，放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，要煮之前才洗。約 2～4 天是工作上限——這是比照嫩葉沙拉菜的公布規則而來，因為沒有人為龍鬚菜本身公布過數字。捲鬚會最先軟掉發褐，判斷新鮮度就看它。袋子不要塞太緊：莖被壓傷後，傷處就會開始變黏。
zh.freezer: 龍鬚菜沒有冷凍保存期限，也不值得冷凍。它的價值全在嫩莖的脆和捲鬚的爽口，而冷凍會把這兩樣都毀掉——解凍後只剩一團濕綠色的東西。這不會不安全，但也沒什麼可以炒了。請買當天晚上就會煮完的份量，這不是適合囤貨的蔬菜。
spoilage: 捲鬚軟垂發褐，尖端接著發黑
莖變得黏滑或發暗，尤其是綁束處
葉子泛黃或變得半透明
打開袋子聞到酸味或發酵味
tips: 挑捲鬚捲得緊、顏色翠綠的，那就是新鮮度測試。
用手折莖，折不斷只是彎曲的那一段就丟掉。
不清洗、鬆鬆裝袋保存，要煮之前才洗。
大火快炒配蒜；久炒會變灰、口感也變滑膩。

faq.q: 龍鬚菜放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏，不清洗、鬆鬆裝在打洞袋裡約 2～4 天。這個數字是比照嫩葉沙拉菜而來，龍鬚菜本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，也沒有意義。冷凍會毀掉捲鬚和嫩莖的脆度，而那正是買它的全部理由。

faq.q: 怎麼看龍鬚菜新不新鮮？
faq.a: 看捲鬚：捲得緊、顏色翠綠就是新鮮；軟垂發褐就是老了。再折一下莖，應該清脆折斷而不是彎曲。
要。每根莖從能乾脆折斷的地方折開；折不斷的那一段不管煮多久都還是老纖維。
